.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 243 PM EDT Saturday...

1. A cold front will move through Monday bringing some chances 
for rain, northwesterly breezes, and a reinforcing shot of 
cooler temperatures.

2. Cold air lingering Wednesday morning will trend seasonably 
mild through the rest of the week. A series of weak fronts will 
bring periodic chances of light rain but no significant events 
are expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 243 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure lingers through Sunday with areas 
of frost expected outside the Champlain Valley tonight with 
clear skies and lighter winds pointing to strong radiational 
cooling. By Sunday, winds shift more southwesterly promoting 
warming with temperatures back around seasonal averages in the 
low to mid 60s. 

A front approaches Sunday night and will move through early 
Monday bringing some light rainfall mainly towards the Canadian 
border. Less than 0.25" is expected with low potential for up to
0.33" over upslope areas in the northern Greens. Winds increase
out of the northwest later Monday with gusts likely in the 
20-30 mph range for many locations especially in the northern 
Champlain Valley and along Lake Champlain. These breezes will 
linger and slowly decrease through Tuesday. Cold air advection 
supports temperatures back into the upper 40s to upper 50s 
Monday through Tuesday. Freezing lows are probable Monday and 
Tuesday nights outside the Champlain and St Lawrence Valleys.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Main impactful weather in the days 4 through 7 
timeframe will be potential for freezing temperatures daybreak 
Wednesday where a strong surface inversion is present. 
Temperatures remain on track be a garden killer where vegetation
remains alive, with exceptions potentially in the northern 
Champlain Valley, particularly in the wide valley that is prone 
to see southerly winds mix to the surface. These winds should 
develop overnight and moderate temperatures substantially after 
initially falling off after sunset, as high pressure shifts to 
our southeast overnight. In contrast, southern/eastern portions 
of the Champlain and Connecticut River Valley will be vulnerable
to colder conditions and frost; the latest probabilities of 
freezing temperatures are near 15-30%. Meanwhile, throughout the
Adirondack region and the remainder of central/eastern Vermont,
those probabilities are about 40-90%. Where winds remain calm 
overnight, temperatures could fall up to a few degrees below 
current forecast values and the lowest of the season so far. 

Consensus in the longer range (Wednesday through Friday night) 
shows somewhat unsettled weather with a closed low near Hudson 
Bay finally departing towards the weekend. This scenario holds a
longwave trough over our region but leaves rain chances higher 
to our north, and likewise in northern portions of northern New 
York and Vermont. Low level flow will initially be southerly 
leading to a warming trend through at least Thursday, but a 
couple of cold fronts will probably pass by to support a cooling
trend towards next weekend. There is typical increasing spread 
in the temperature range each day, associated with timing and 
magnitude differences in the air mass change with any front. 
Overall, temperatures will are expected to be fairly typical of 
this time of year regardless of variability. As we get closer to
next weekend the details will become sharper with regards to 
these fluctuations.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 00Z Monday...Mainly VFR conditions will continue. The 
only potential impacts through the period will be related to 
radiation fog. Periods of dense fog will likely result after 
about 06Z at SLK, MPV, and EFK. With much drier air in place 
this afternoon compared to yesterday, it will take more time for
fog to form but temperatures are favored to drop well below 
crossover values. As the center of high pressure moves to the 
northeast of the airspace overnight, low level southeasterly 
flow develops and could disrupt fog at MPV and have ended fog a 
bit earlier there compared to EFK. Following 12Z, increasing 
southerly flow will occur, leading to winds at Champlain Valley 
terminals gusting near or a bit above 20 knots, while EFK and 
MPV see sustained winds also reach 10-12 knots with somewhat 
lighter winds at SLK and MSS.
